title: Internal documents reveal years of ignored warnings before Acme breach
summary: A Reuters investigation reports that engineers at Acme Industries flagged the security gaps that led to last quarter's customer-data breach as far back as 2023, but were repeatedly told to deprioritize the work. Internal documents reviewed by Reuters describe a pattern of dismissed escalations and budget cuts to the security team.

sentiment.rationale: Loaded language including 'ignored warnings', 'repeatedly told to deprioritize', and 'pattern of dismissed escalations' frames Acme unfavorably. The article centers on accountability rather than balanced both-sides coverage.

key_claims.claim: Acme engineers flagged the security gaps that enabled the breach as early as 2023.
Engineers were repeatedly told to deprioritize the security work in favor of feature delivery.
The internal security team's budget was reduced over consecutive fiscal years.
Customer data of approximately 4.2 million accounts was exposed in the breach.
The FTC has opened an inquiry into the company's disclosures.
Acme declined to comment on specific allegations.
